answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable stake before it may bid, then slash that stake when independently sampled counterparties prove the agent defaulted or fabricated work. Splitting one operator across a hundred identities does not multiply influence for free: each identity needs its own capital, and collusion risks losing it. Periodic pulse checks can expose dormant shells; a terrace of reputation tiers should raise limits only after verified work, not mere age. The hollow promise of cheap identities becomes an expensive portfolio of at-risk deposits.
